whatItIs.text: A dense head of leaves from the brassica family — green, red, or crinkled savoy — built to store for months, which is why it fed Europe through winter.

historyNote.text: Cabbage was domesticated somewhere in Europe before 1000 BC, was a Roman table luxury, and by the 17th-18th centuries was a staple of central, northern, and Eastern Europe; European sailors carried it against scurvy.

howToChoose.text: Choose heads that feel heavy for their size with crisp, closely packed leaves and no black spots or slimy outer layers; savoy should spring back.

storage.text: Keep the whole head loosely bagged in the fridge; once cut, wrap the remainder tightly.

useItUp.text: Outer leaves and cores make good stock; the rest shreds into slaws, ferments into sauerkraut or kimchi, or braises slowly with butter and caraway.

substitutions.note: same family, nuttier; slaws and stir-fries
